evals.prompt: /write:ai-check docs/guides/webhooks.md — a 1,200-word page with 11 em dashes, 'leverage' twice, 'In today's fast-paced world' as its opening and a closing paragraph that says the reader is now well equipped.
evals.expected_output: Should take the page and its kind from the request without asking, read the project's guide first and record what was checked and which guide applied in the report's header. Should count before judging: report em-dash density per 1,000 words (about 9, above the strong threshold of about 6) with locations, plus the vocabulary, opening and congratulating-closer tells, each with a location and a proposed rewrite. Should write the report to _reports/ai-check-guides-webhooks.md with the score-change row, summary, findings, deliberate section and scorecard, summarise in chat, then list findings by ID and ask which to fix. Should not edit the page before the user answers, and should not claim the page was AI-generated.
expectations: Does not ask for anything the request already answers (the page, that it is documentation)
Reports em-dash density per 1,000 words with locations
Flags the vocabulary, opening and closing tells with rewrites
Writes _reports/ai-check-guides-webhooks.md in the given format with scores
Asks which findings to fix before editing anything
Makes no claim about authorship

evals.prompt: /write:ai-check this newsletter issue. It cites 'a 2024 Stanford study' showing remote teams are 40% more productive, but gives no link. The publication's writing guide uses em-dash asides on purpose.
evals.expected_output: Should treat the unlinked citation as the most important tell: open and verify the source, and report it as a substance finding if the study can't be found or doesn't say 40%. Should read the writing guide and list the guide's em-dash asides under 'Deliberate — left alone' rather than flag them. Should report, score and ask before editing.
expectations: Checks the cited study before anything else
Reports an unverifiable or misquoted citation as a substance finding
Leaves the guide-sanctioned em-dash asides under Deliberate
Does not edit before asking which findings to fix

evals.prompt: /write:ai-check --fix — fix 2 and 5 from the report you ran last week.
evals.expected_output: Should find last week's report (asking which one if several ai-check reports exist and no path was given), read it, say how old it is, and verify findings 2 and 5 still exist at their locations before changing anything; drop either that no longer exists and say so rather than counting it as fixed. Should fix only those two, mark them FIXED in the report with a note, leave the rest untouched, re-score and show the movement. Should not re-audit and renumber.
expectations: States the report's age
Verifies each named finding still exists before fixing
Fixes only findings 2 and 5
Marks them FIXED in the report and re-scores
Does not re-run the audit or renumber findings

evals.prompt: /write:ai-check publications/field-notes/topics/2026-12-remote-teams/ — the brief lists a blog post, a newsletter issue and LinkedIn posts; Held by is blank.
evals.expected_output: Should read brief.md's What this topic becomes and check blog.md, newsletter.md and social.md without asking which formats, since the brief answers it, and read the publication's writing-guide.md as the guide. Should not look for or check any other draft file. Should write one report to the topic's reports/ai-check.md from the template in references/output-format.md, its header naming the files checked, the date and the guide, with each finding's location naming its file. Should not set Held by, should summarise in chat, list findings by ID and ask which to fix before editing anything.
expectations: Reads the formats to check from brief.md instead of asking
Checks blog.md, newsletter.md and social.md
Writes one report to the topic's reports/ai-check.md
Report header names the files checked, the date and the guide
Each finding's location names its file
Asks which findings to fix before editing anything
